title: Prostate Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for prostate cancer. Full pathway: initial workup -> disease state -> (localized risk group / mCSPC volume / mCRPC biomarker + line of therapy) -> treatment with per-node checklists -> surveillance and biochemical-recurrence pathways. Each treatment leaf routes to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference (same disease-stage scope only); modalities/agents without a dose protocol (active surveillance, radiation, surgery, apalutamide/darolutamide, pembrolizumab MSI-H, radium-223) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup/risk-stratification/staging/surveillance content is standard oncology, not proprietary guideline text; structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate Cancer, no proprietary content reproduced. Invents no dose/regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers; the dose engine computes patient doses.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and risk assessment
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation before treatment. Confirm histology, establish grade group and clinical stage, and stratify risk.

bullets.label: History and physical, including digital rectal exam (DRE)
bullets.sub: performance status, symptoms, family cancer history

bullets.label: Prostate biopsy: ISUP grade group / Gleason score, number and % of positive cores
Risk stratification: PSA, grade group, clinical T stage, % positive cores
Staging imaging by risk
bullets.sub: bone scan + CT/MRI, or PSMA-PET (higher sensitivity) for unfavorable-intermediate risk and above / on biochemical recurrence

bullets.label: Germline testing (BRCA1/2, HRR, MMR) if high-risk, node-positive, metastatic, or strong family history
Consider a tumor genomic classifier (e.g. Decipher) to refine localized risk
Assess bone health and comorbidity before androgen-deprivation therapy

nodes.name: Disease state
nodes.title: Disease state
nodes.description: Prostate cancer management is defined first by disease state. Choose the current clinical state.

nodes.name: Localized risk group
nodes.title: Localized: risk group
nodes.description: Stratify localized / regional disease by risk group. Risk group drives whether, and how long, systemic therapy is added to local therapy.

bullets.label: Favorable intermediate
bullets.sub: grade group 1-2, PSA 10-20 or cT2b-c, and < 50% positive cores

bullets.label: Unfavorable intermediate
bullets.sub: grade group 3, or two-plus intermediate factors, or >= 50% positive cores

bullets.label: High / very-high
bullets.sub: PSA > 20, grade group 4-5, cT3-4, or regional node-positive (N1)

nodes.name: Active surveillance
nodes.title: Very-low / low risk: active surveillance
nodes.description: Preferred for very-low and low-risk disease. Monitor and reserve definitive local therapy for reclassification. No systemic therapy.
bullets: PSA every 6 months; DRE every 12 months
Multiparametric MRI and confirmatory / repeat biopsy at 6-12 months, then per protocol
Definitive therapy (radical prostatectomy or radiation) on grade or volume reclassification
Radical prostatectomy or radiation are alternatives for patients who prefer treatment

nodes.name: Favorable intermediate
nodes.title: Favorable intermediate: local therapy
nodes.description: Definitive local therapy; short-course ADT is generally NOT required. Active surveillance remains an option for selected patients.
bullets: External-beam radiation (EBRT) or brachytherapy - ADT usually not added
Radical prostatectomy + pelvic lymph-node dissection if nomogram node risk is meaningful
Active surveillance for selected patients
If radiation is combined with ADT, the ADT backbone regimen is referenced below

nodes.name: Unfavorable intermediate
nodes.title: Unfavorable intermediate: RT + short-term ADT
nodes.description: Radiation with short-term androgen-deprivation therapy, or surgery.
bullets: EBRT + short-term ADT (about 4-6 months); brachytherapy boost is an option
Radical prostatectomy + pelvic lymph-node dissection
Consider adjuvant / early-salvage radiation after prostatectomy for adverse pathology
ADT backbone regimen referenced below

nodes.name: High / very-high risk
nodes.title: High / very-high risk: RT + long-term ADT (intensified)
nodes.description: Multimodal therapy. Radiation with long-term ADT is standard; intensify for very-high-risk / node-positive disease.
bullets: EBRT + long-term ADT (about 18-36 months); EBRT + brachytherapy boost is an option
Add abiraterone to ADT for very-high-risk / node-positive disease (intensification)
Radical prostatectomy + extended pelvic lymph-node dissection in selected candidates (multimodal)
Manage bone health during long-term ADT
ADT backbone regimen referenced below; abiraterone is an mCRPC-scoped protocol here so it is listed as guidance

nodes.name: Recurrence setting
nodes.title: Biochemical recurrence: prior local therapy
nodes.description: Rising PSA after prior definitive local therapy. Restage (PSMA-PET where available); management differs by the primary treatment received.
bullets: Confirm rising PSA and calculate PSA doubling-time
PSMA-PET (or CT + bone scan) to distinguish local vs regional vs distant recurrence

nodes.name: BCR after prostatectomy
nodes.title: BCR after prostatectomy: salvage radiation +/- ADT
nodes.description: Localized recurrence after surgery.
bullets: Salvage radiation to the prostate bed +/- pelvic nodes, ideally at low PSA
Add ADT to salvage radiation for higher-risk features
Observation if PSA doubling-time is long and life expectancy limited
If PSMA-PET shows distant disease, treat as metastatic (mCSPC pathway)

nodes.name: BCR after radiation
nodes.title: BCR after radiation: local salvage vs ADT
nodes.description: Recurrence after primary radiation.
bullets: Biopsy to confirm local recurrence; restage with PSMA-PET
Local salvage (salvage prostatectomy, cryotherapy, HIFU, or brachytherapy) for confirmed local-only recurrence
ADT for regional / distant recurrence or non-candidates for local salvage
Observation if PSA doubling-time is long
ADT backbone regimen referenced below

nodes.name: nmCRPC
nodes.title: nmCRPC (M0 CRPC): continue ADT + next-generation ARPI
nodes.description: Non-metastatic castration-resistant disease. Confirm castrate testosterone; the driver is a short PSA doubling-time.
bullets: Confirm castrate testosterone (< 50 ng/dL) and M0 status (PSMA-PET may reclassify to metastatic)
For PSA doubling-time <= 10 months: continue ADT and add apalutamide, darolutamide, or enzalutamide to delay metastasis
Apalutamide / darolutamide have no dedicated dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance (same ARPI class)
Bone-health monitoring on continued ADT
Enzalutamide dose protocol referenced below (same drug class)

nodes.name: mCSPC volume
nodes.title: mCSPC: metastatic burden
nodes.description: In metastatic castration-sensitive disease, volume and de-novo vs recurrent presentation guide how intensively to escalate ADT. ADT alone is no longer preferred.

bullets.label: High-volume
bullets.sub: visceral metastases and/or >= 4 bone metastases with >= 1 beyond the vertebral column / pelvis

bullets: Start ADT backbone in all; add at least one intensification agent

nodes.name: mCSPC triplet
nodes.title: mCSPC (high-volume): ADT + docetaxel + ARPI (triplet)
nodes.description: High-volume / de-novo disease in fit patients.
bullets: Triplet: ADT + docetaxel + an ARPI (abiraterone or darolutamide) for fit patients
ADT + ARPI doublet is an acceptable alternative if docetaxel is not suitable
Bone-supportive therapy for bone metastases; continue ADT indefinitely
Component regimens referenced below

nodes.name: mCSPC doublet
nodes.title: mCSPC (low-volume): ADT + ARPI doublet
nodes.description: Low-volume disease.
bullets: ADT + an ARPI (abiraterone, apalutamide, or enzalutamide)
Radiation to the primary is an option for low-volume disease
Bone-supportive therapy for bone metastases; continue ADT indefinitely
ADT + ARPI regimen referenced below

nodes.name: mCRPC option
nodes.title: mCRPC: biomarker / burden
nodes.description: In mCRPC, select the directing feature. Obtain HRR (germline + somatic), MMR/MSI, and PSMA-PET where available.
bullets: Confirm castrate testosterone before labelling castration-resistant
Test HRR (BRCA1/2, ATM...), MMR/MSI (or TMB), and PSMA-PET status
Prior therapy guides sequencing (avoid ARPI-to-ARPI switching)

nodes.name: mCRPC line
nodes.title: mCRPC: line of therapy
nodes.description: Sequencing in mCRPC without an actionable biomarker depends on what was already given in the castration-sensitive setting.

nodes.name: mCRPC first line
nodes.title: mCRPC, no prior ARPI/taxane: ARPI or docetaxel
nodes.description: Treatment-naive mCRPC.
bullets: An ARPI (abiraterone + prednisone, or enzalutamide) is preferred for most
Docetaxel for symptomatic / rapidly progressive or visceral disease
Sipuleucel-T is an option for asymptomatic / minimally symptomatic disease (no dose protocol here)
Continue ADT; maintain bone health

nodes.name: mCRPC post-ARPI
nodes.title: mCRPC after an ARPI: taxane (switch class)
nodes.description: Progression on a prior ARPI. Avoid ARPI-to-ARPI switching where possible.
bullets: Docetaxel is preferred (switch mechanism of action)
PSMA-radioligand (if PSMA-positive) or a PARP inhibitor (if HRR-altered) are biomarker options
Re-test HRR / MSI / PSMA if not already done
Continue ADT; maintain bone health

nodes.name: mCRPC post-taxane
nodes.title: mCRPC after docetaxel: cabazitaxel / next options
nodes.description: Progression after docetaxel.
bullets: Cabazitaxel + steroid (post-docetaxel taxane)
An ARPI if not previously used; PSMA-radioligand if PSMA-positive; PARP inhibitor if HRR-altered
Radium-223 for symptomatic bone-predominant disease without visceral spread
Continue ADT; maintain bone health

nodes.name: mCRPC PARP
nodes.title: mCRPC, HRR / BRCA: PARP inhibitor
nodes.description: mCRPC with a homologous-recombination-repair or BRCA1/2 alteration.
bullets: A PARP inhibitor (olaparib), typically after or combined with an ARPI
Confirm the HRR / BRCA alteration (germline and/or somatic)
Continue ADT; maintain bone health

nodes.name: mCRPC immunotherapy
nodes.title: mCRPC, MSI-H / dMMR: immunotherapy
nodes.description: Microsatellite-instability-high or mismatch-repair-deficient mCRPC.
bullets: Pembrolizumab under the tissue-agnostic MSI-H / dMMR indication
No prostate-specific dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance (physician arranges the pembrolizumab regimen)
Continue ADT; maintain bone health

nodes.name: mCRPC radioligand
nodes.title: mCRPC, PSMA-positive: radioligand therapy
nodes.description: mCRPC with PSMA-positive imaging, typically after an ARPI and a taxane.
bullets: Lu-177-PSMA (PSMA-617) radioligand therapy
Requires PSMA-positive imaging and adequate marrow / renal function
Continue ADT; maintain bone health

nodes.name: mCRPC radium-223
nodes.title: mCRPC, bone-predominant: radium-223
nodes.description: Symptomatic bone-predominant mCRPC without visceral disease.
bullets: Radium-223 (alpha-emitter): prolongs survival, reduces symptomatic skeletal events
Not combined with abiraterone + prednisone
No dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance (physician arranges the regimen)
Add a bone-modifying agent (denosumab or zoledronic acid) for skeletal protection

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Monitoring cadence after definitive or systemic therapy; escalate on PSA rise.
bullets: After definitive local therapy: PSA every 6-12 months for 5 years, then annually; DRE annually
A confirmed rising PSA defines biochemical recurrence - restage (PSMA-PET) and enter the recurrence pathway
On systemic therapy: PSA + testosterone, symptom and imaging assessment at intervals; watch for castration resistance
Ongoing bone-health monitoring and cardiovascular / metabolic care during ADT
